title: Spaghetti Bolognese
subtitle: Slow-cooked Italian meat ragù with spaghetti
excerpt: A long-cooked ragù of beef and pork mince with wine, tomatoes, and milk, served with spaghetti and Parmesan. The most copied Italian dish in the world, best made properly.

recipe.sourceNotes: Ragù alla bolognese is the meat sauce from Bologna in northern Italy. The authentic recipe was registered with the Bologna Chamber of Commerce in 1982 and specifies beef, pancetta, onion, carrot, celery, tomato paste, white wine, and milk. The British and American version (spaghetti bolognese) is almost universally prepared with a much higher proportion of tomatoes and without milk, producing a completely different, more acidic sauce. The milk in the traditional version is added to soften the acidity of the tomatoes and to give the sauce a richer, more rounded flavour. The sauce must cook for at least 2 hours to fully develop: a ragù cooked for 30 minutes is acceptable but not the same thing. In Bologna, the sauce is served with tagliatelle, never spaghetti. Spaghetti bolognese is an Anglo-American invention.

recipeTools.notes: A wide, heavy-based saucepan or casserole.

content.text: Brown the mince in batches over high heat until deeply coloured, not grey. A saucepan full of grey, steaming mince has not developed any flavour; a saucepan of browned mince has. The soffritto (onion, carrot, celery) must be cooked slowly and completely before the meat is added. Add the milk about halfway through cooking: the sauce should look rich and creamy when it is finished, not watery and tomato-red.

Heat the oil in a wide heavy saucepan over medium-low heat. Fry the lardons for 3 minutes. Add the onion, carrot, and celery and cook for 12 minutes until completely soft. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.

Increase to high heat. Add the beef and pork mince in batches, browning thoroughly. Return all the mince. Add the tomato puree and cook for 2 minutes. Pour in the red wine and cook until almost evaporated, about 5 minutes.

Add the tinned tomatoes, stock, bay leaves, salt, and pepper. Bring to a simmer. Reduce to the lowest heat. Cook uncovered for 1 hour 30 minutes, stirring occasionally. Add the milk after the first hour. The sauce should be thick and rich, not liquid.

Cook the pasta in well-salted boiling water according to packet instructions until al dente. Reserve a cup of pasta water before draining. Toss the pasta with the ragù, adding a splash of pasta water to loosen if needed. Serve with grated Parmesan.
